 3 SCCH-24  MVC No.2964/2015  JUDGEMENT This claim petition is filed by the petitioners under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming the compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- on account of the death of Sri. Narayan Parida in the Motor Vehicles Accident.

2. The case of the petitioners are as under :
The 1st petitioner is the wife and 2nd and 3rd petitioners are the sons of deceased Narayan Parida.

That on 15.05.2015 at about 10.30 a.m., near Pizza Hut, G.B. Palya,
Hosur Main Road, when the deceased was about to cross the road, a two wheeler bearing Reg.No.KA-05-JD-5532 came rashly and negligently without caring for human safety and dashed against the deceased.
Due to impact the deceased fell down and sustained blood injuries all over the body and died on the spot.

Postmortem was conducted at NIMHANS, thereafter the body was handed over to the petitioners for 4 SCCH-24 MVC No.2964/2015 performing the last rites and the petitioners have spent more than Rs.1,00,000/- towards the transportation of dead body and performing last rites.
3. It is submitted that, the deceased was hale and healthy before his death, working as an Assistant Supervisor in G4S Secure Solution (India) Pvt. Ltd., and earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.
He had very good future prospects and his salary would also rise.

Further submitted that, the deceased is only the bread earner in the family and all the family members depends on him for their Minali Parida vs Kiran Kumar on 27 February, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90583259/
2 food, clothing and shelter.

sentences.text: Due to the accident, the petitioners have lost the earnings of the deceased and the 1st petitioner has lost her loving husband and the 2nd and 3rd petitioners have lost their caring and supportive father and they have put into great agony, pain, frustration and deep mental stress.

The complaint has been lodged in the Madiwala Traffic police 5 SCCH-24 MVC No.2964/2015 Station in their Crime No.77/2015 for the offences punishable under section 279,
304(A) of IPC against the rash and negligent driving of the vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-D-5532.
The respondent who is the owner of the said vehicle is liable to pay the compensation.
Hence, the petitioners pray to award the compensation with interest at the rate of 12% per annum.
4. After service of notice, the respondent has not appeared before this Tribunal.
Hence respondent has been placed Ex-parte.

5. On the basis of the above pleadings of the petitioners, the following points arises for my consideration :-
POINTS 1.
Whether the petitioners prove that they are the legal representatives of the deceased Narayan Parida?

6 SCCH-24 MVC No.2964/2015 2. Whether the petitioners prove that the deceased Narayan Parida had died due to the injuries sustained in the road traffic accident that occurred on 15.05.2015 at about 10.30 a.m., near Pizza Hut, G.B. Palya, Hosur Main Road, due to the rash and negligent driving of the two wheeler bearing Reg.No.KA- 05-JD -5532 by its rider as alleged?
3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for the compensation as claimed?

If so, to what amount and from whom?
4.What order or Award ?

6 . In order to substantiate the case made out by the petitioners, the 2nd petitioner got himself examined as P.W.1 and one witness has been examined as P.W.2 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.16.
Thereafter, the petitioners closed their side evidence.
7. Heard the arguments.
Perused the materials placed on record.

My findings on the above Points are as under:
Point No.1 - In the Affirmative. Point No.2 - In the Affirmative.
Point No.3 - Partly in the Affirmative.

The petitioners are entitled for a total compensation of Rs.11,36,548/-.
From respondent.
Point No.4 - As per final order.
The case of the petitioners is that, the 1st petitioner is the wife, 2nd and 3rd petitioners are the sons of deceased Narayan Parida.
In order to substantiate the said facts, P.W.1 the 2nd petitioner has entered into witness box and by filing affidavit has deposed about their relationship with the deceased.

In order to substantiate the said facts, P.W.1 has produced Ex.P.11 to Ex.P.13 i.e., copy of the Aadhaar Cards of 2nd 8 SCCH-24 MVC No.2964/2015 petitioner, copy of Ration Card and copy of Election Identity card of the 2nd petitioner.
Ex. P.11
to 13 and other materials on record discloses the relationship of petitioners with deceased Narayan Parida.
The relationship of the petitioners and the deceased was undisputed as the respondent remained Ex-parte.

Under such circumstances,
there is no need to discuss much on the relationship of petitioners with the deceased.
Hence, I answer Point No.1 in the Affirmative.

POINT No.2:
10.

It is the case of the petitioners that, on 15.05.2015 at about 10.30 a.m., near Pizza Hut, G.B. Palya, Hosur Main Road, when the deceased was about to cross the road, a two wheeler bearing Reg.No.KA-05- JD-5532 came rashly and negligently without caring for human safety and dashed against the deceased.
Due to impact the deceased fell down and sustained bleeding 9 SCCH-24 MVC No.2964/2015 injuries all over the body and died on the spot.

According to the petitioners the said accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the two wheeler bearing Reg.No.KA-05-JD-5532 and in this regard the Madiwala Police have registered a case in Crime No.77/2015 for the offences punishable under Section 279, 337 and 304A of Indian Penal Code.
11. In order to prove the actionable negligence, the petitioner No.2 has entered into the witness box and got examined himself as P.W.1.
He reiterates the averments and allegations made in the claim petition.
In support of their evidence petitioners have examined P.W.2 the H.R. Leader in G4S Secure Solutions (India) Pvt. Ltd., Bengaluru.
P.W.2 deposed that, Narayan Parida had expired in the road traffic accident on 15.05.2015 while in service, who was working in their company since 26.08.2008 as a Security Guard.

The evidence of P.W.1 10 SCCH-24 MVC No.2964/2015 and P.W.2 remained unchallenged as the respondent remained Ex-parte.
12.
The petitioners have relied upon the police documents produced at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.10.

Out of these documents Ex.P.1 is copy of the First Information Report, Ex.P.2 is copy of the Complaint,
Ex.P.3 is copy of the Post Mortem Report and Ex.P.4 is copy of the Inquest Report, Ex.P.5 is copy of the Mahazar, Ex.P.6 is copy of the Police Intimation, Ex.P.7 is copy of the IMV Report, Ex.P.8 is Minali Parida vs Kiran Kumar on 27 February, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90583259/
4 copy of the Sketch, Ex.P.9 is copy of the Charge Sheet and Ex.P.10 is Death Certificate.

Ex.P.1, i.e.
the First Information Report, which discloses that a criminal case has been registered against the driver of the Motor Cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-JD-5532 for the offences punishable under section 279, 337 and 304A of the Indian Penal Code. After investigation the police have filed the charge sheet against the driver of the said motor 11 SCCH-24 MVC No.2964/2015 cycle for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 304A of Indian Penal Code and Section 146 r/w 196 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act.
Ex.P.5 i.e., the copy of Spot Mahazar and Ex.
P.8 i.e.
, the copy of Sketch drawn on the seen of the occurrence supports the case of the petitioners.
Thus, the contents Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.10 prima- facie establishes the rash or negligence on the part of the rider of the Motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-JD -5532.
In this case the respondent remained Ex-parte.
Hence, the evidence of P.W.1 and the contents of police documents remained unrebutted and unchallenged.

Under these circumstances, the evidence of P.W.1, coupled with the contents of the police documents, establishes that the accident has occurred solely due to the rash and negligent riding of the Motor Cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-JD-5532 by it's rider and the deceased Narayana Parida has died due to injuries sustained in 12 SCCH-24 MVC No.2964/2015 the said accident.

Accordingly,
Point No.2 is answered in the Affirmative.

POINT No.3 :
13.
The petitioners are claiming compensation on account of the death of the Narayana Parida in the said road traffic accident.

It is stated in the claim petition as well as in the evidence by P.W.1 that the deceased was working as an Assignment Supervisor G4S Secure Solution Pvt. Ltd., and he was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
P.W.1 deposed that, all the family members were depending on the deceased for their food, clothing, shelter and now their lives are put into dark.
In order to substantiate the avocation and earnings of the deceased the petitioners have examined P.W.2 Bhaskar H.R. the H.R. Leader in G4S Secure Solutions (India) Pvt. Ltd., Bengaluru.
P.W.2 deposed that, the deceased Narayana 13 SCCH-24 MVC No.2964/2015 Parida was working in their company since 26.08.2008 as a Security Guard and he was drawing salary of Rs.9,703.88 ps. Per month.

In support of his evidence P.W.2 has produced Ex.P.14 i.e., Authorization Letter, Ex.P.15 i.e.,
Appointment Letter of deceased Narayan Parida and Ex.
, the 3 Pay Slips.
Ex . P.15
show shows that, the deceased Narayana Parida was appointed as a Security Guard on 26.08.2008 and his rates of wages was Rs.3,020/- per month.

In Ex.P.16 the pay slip for the month of February-2015 shows the standard salary of the deceased was Rs.9,703.88n and the calculated salary was Rs.6,777.95 paid/120 hours, in the month of April-2015 standard salary is shown as Rs.8,806/- and calculated salary was Rs.4,236.15/80 hours and in the month of May-2015 standard salary is Rs.10,084/- and calculated salary was Rs.6,656.65/112 hours.
Except these salary slips the petitioners have not produced any other materials to show that, deceased 14 SCCH-24 MVC No.2964/2015 Narayana Parida was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
But it is clear that, Narayana Parida was working as a Security Guard in G4S Secure Solutions Pvt.Ltd., Bengaluru.

Therefore,
taking into the consideration of the present day condition and the documents produced by the petitioners, it is difficult to arrive that Narayana Parida was earning Rs.20,000/- per month as contended by the petitioners.
Under the above circumstances, if the income of the deceased is inferred at Rs.8,000/- per month that would meet the ends of justice.

5 14.
In the decision reported in 2013 ACJ 1403 between Rajesh and others V/s. Rajbir Singh and others.

entities.text: 2013 ACJ 1403 between Rajesh and others V/s. Rajbir Singh and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Wherein it is held that :
"Quantum-Fatal accident- Principles of assessment - Future prospects- Whether formula for increase of income for future prospects adopted for person with permanent jobs in Sarla Verma's case 2009 ACJ 1298(SC) may also be applied to 15 SCCH-24 MVC No.2964/2015 persons who were self employed or were engaged on fixed wages - Held :
yes : 50 percent of actual income (after deduction of tax) for persons below 40 years 30 percent for the age group of 40 to 50 years.
15 percent for age group of 50 to 60 years; but no addition thereafter".

On perusal of the above cited decision it is clear that, 50 percent of actual income (after deduction of tax) for the persons below 40 years and 30 percent for the age group of 40 to 50 years 15 percent for age group of 50 to 60 years is to be added.
15. The income of the deceased is considered as Rs.8,000/- per month.
As per the petition the deceased was aged about 48 years at the time of his death.
The Post Mortem Report at Ex.P.3 shows the age of the deceased was 48 years at the time of his death.
Ex. P.15
the Appointment Order show the date of birth of the deceased as 20.04.1966.
The petitioners have not 16 SCCH-24 MVC No.2964/2015 produced any authenticated document to show the correct age of deceased at the time of accident.
Under such circumstances the age of deceased is taken as 49 years as on the date of accident.
As per above cited decision, 30% of the income of the deceased is to be added to his monthly income.

Then, it comes (Rs.8,000+Rs.2,400/-) to Rs.10,400/-
per month.
Admittedly, the deceased was a married person and having wife as the only dependent.
The petitioners No.2 and 3 are major sons and having their own income.
Thus, as per the decision reported in Sarala Verma case, 1/3rd of the income is to be deducted towards his personal and living expenses.

Thereby, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that, the monthly income of the deceased is to be considered as (Rs.10,400/- - Rs.3,467/-)= Rs.6,933/- per month and Rs.83,196/-
per annum.
The income of the deceased is below the taxable limits.
As per the decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 17 SCCH-24 MVC No.2964/2015 between Sarala Verma & Others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and others the appropriate multiplier is '13'.

entities.text: Sarala Verma & Others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: So the loss of dependency works out to (Rs.6,933/- X 12 X 13) = Rs.10,81,548/-.
Thus, a sum of Rs.10,81,548/- is awarded under the head loss of dependency.
16. In the case on hand, the petitioner No.1 is the wife of the deceased, who has lost her husband, the companion and life partner.
Taking into consideration of the said fact, this Tribunal is of the considered view that it would be just and proper to award a compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards loss of consortium.

sentences.text: In this case, petitioner No.2 and petitioner No.3 are the sons of the deceased Narayana Parida.
They have lost love and affection of the deceased.

Taking into consideration of the said fact, this Tribunal is of the 18 SCCH-24 MVC No.2964/2015 considered view that, it would be just and proper to award a compensation of Rs.20,000/- under the head loss of love and affection.
18. It is the evidence of P.W.1 that, they have spent Rs.1,50,000/- towards transportation of dead body to their native and performing last rites.
It is pertinent to note that, the petitioners basically from the state of Orissa and must have spent money towards transportation of body from the Hospital to resident.
No doubt petitioners must have spent money for funeral and obsequies ceremony.

Hence, in the absence of proof, a sum of Rs.15,000/- is awarded towards Transportation,
Funeral and obsequies ceremony.

Accordingly the petitioners are granted with the compensation under the following heads :
19 SCCH-24 MVC No.2964/2015 1. Loss of dependency.

Rs. 10,81,548/-
2. Loss of consortium.

3. Loss of love and Rs. 20,000/-
affection.

4. Transportation, Rs. 15,000/-
Funeral and obsequies ceremony.

Total Rs. 11,36,548/-
So, the petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.11,36,548/-(Rupees Eleven Lakhs Thirty Six Thousand Five Hundred and Forty Eight only) with interest at the rate of 8% per annum from the date of petition, till the date of realisation.
19 . It is held supra by this Tribunal that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the Motor Cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-JD-5532 by its rider.

Admittedly respondent did not appear before this tribunal to challenge the petition nor tried to produce documents to show that his vehicle was covered with any insurance policy as on the date of accident.
According to petition averments the offending vehicle was not having any insurance policy.
This aspect is not at all disputed by the respondent.
Under such circumstances the respondent being the R.C. owner of the above said Motor Cycle is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
Accordingly, Point No.3 is answered partly in the Affirmative.

POINT No.4:

sentences.text: For the foregoing reasons and the discussions as stated above, the petition filed by the petitioners deserves to be allowed in part with costs.

In result, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Petition filed under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act by the petitioners is hereby allowed in part with costs.

The petitioners are awarded a total compensation of Rs.11,36,548/-
21 SCCH-24 MVC No.2964/2015 (Rupees Eleven Lakhs Thirty Six Thousand Five Hundred and Forty Eight only) with interest at the rate of 8% per annum from the date of petition, till deposit.
The Respondents is liable to pay the compensation awarded in this case to the petitioners.
The Respondent shall deposit the said compensation amount into the Tribunal within 60 days from the date of this order.

Out of the compensation award amount, the petitioner No.1 is entitled for a sum of Rs.10,36,548/- ,
the petitioner No.2 is entitled for a sum of Rs.50,000/- and the petitioner No.3 is entitled for a sum of Rs.50,000/- with proportionate interest.
Out of the compensation awarded 50% of the award amount of the 1st petitioner shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in her name in any of the Nationalised Bank or Scheduled Bank for a period of 5 years free from encumbrance with liberty to draw the accrued periodical interest.
The remaining compensation amount shall be disbursed to the petitioner No.1.

The entire compensation amount with accrued interest shall be  22 SCCH-24  MVC No.2964/2015 disbursed to the petitioners No.2 and 3 respectively.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw award accordingly.
(Dictated to the stenographer directly on Computer, typed by her, corrected by me and then pronounced in the open court on this the 27th day of February, 2017).
